result:
**Opening argument (Debater A): stack(C_n) = n(2^{n-1} − 1) + 1**

The expression I defend, (2^{n-1}·n − n) + 1, is algebraically identical to n(2^{n-1} − 1) + 1 = n·2^{n-1} − n + 1, the formula Debater B argues for. We agree on the value, so the disagreement is only about the justification.

The solution supports this value in three steps:

1. **Lower bound (unsolvable configuration).** The uniform configuration p_i = 2^{n-1} − 1 has total N = n(2^{n-1} − 1). Here A_t ≡ 1 (mod 2^{n-1}), so every target fails: p_t + q_t + 2r_t = 2^n − 1 < 2^n. Thus stack(C_n) > n(2^{n-1} − 1).

2. **Upper bound (counting).** Summing the failure conditions over all targets gives N + R ≤ n·2^{n-1}, where R = Σr_t ≥ n. Hence any unsolvable configuration has N ≤ n(2^{n-1} − 1), so n(2^{n-1} − 1) + 1 pebbles always suffice.

3. **Independent check.** For C_2, the configuration (1,1) is unsolvable and every 3-pebble configuration is solvable. The formula gives 2·(2−1)+1 = 3. ✓

Both bounds meet at n(2^{n-1} − 1) + 1, so this is the exact stacking number.
